comment: Frozen normalisation table for the fleet session graph (ADR 0096 decision 3).
`raw` is a live-state string as it arrives; `state` is the LedgerState written
and read; `band` is the SegmentKind it paints (types/fleetgraph.ts).
Two implementations exist — the Agent writes the ledger in Go, the builder
normalises the live sessions map in TypeScript — so BOTH test suites read THIS
file. A test that cannot find it must fail, not skip: a silently skipped parity
check and a passing one look identical.
Matching is exact. No case folding, no trimming: these strings are produced by
code, and folding would quietly accept a spelling nobody writes.
`raw: null` is the one input the two sides do NOT share: Session.state is
optional, so the TypeScript side receives undefined for a live session whose
hooks have not reported yet, while Go only ever sees "". It means the same as
"" — idle. Falling it through to `unknown` would hatch every running session
